text:
derek: Heads-up — TTFT on /chat-stream jumped ~25% after the kernel-selector change last Wednesday. p95 token latency moved from ~1.6s -> ~2.1s during the window. Seeing a cluster-wide pattern, not just one host. Anyone tracking kernel handoffs?

marta: Which time window? p95 vs p99? Is this only in hosted or also dedicated?

derek: Window 2026-03-14 02:00–03:00 UTC. p95 up, p99 also shifted but noisier. Both hosted and a subset of dedicated pools affected.

elya: Quick finding from a local perf replay: batch-shape histogram shifted toward smaller batches (more 1-4 token batches). The selector started choosing the tiled-matmul kernel for many seq_len=1024 requests because the shape-matcher rule missed quantized-kernel compatibility. That path has higher kernel-setup cost.

simon: I correlated KV cache telemetry — miss rate on /chat-stream jumped from ~3% -> ~18% in the same window. If KV misses cause additional decoding and KV unpack, TTFT will include that extra work.

perf-bot: Automated profiling summary (trimmed):
  - top token-phase time: kernel-setup 34%, decode 41%, kv-unpack 12%, scheduling 8%
  - dominant kernel: tiled-matmul (setup heavy) vs fused-matmul (faster steady-state)
  - note: small-batch overheads visible in tcp traces

marta: Proposal for instrumentation (minimal, actionable):
  1) Add token-level phase label: phase in {ttft, decode, kernel-setup, kernel-exec, kv-unpack, prequeue}.
  2) Kernel name label: kernel_name (e.g., fused-matmul, tiled-matmul, cuBLAS, quant-fused).
  3) Batch shape labels: batch_tokens and seq_len (or a single shape tag like "b=4_s=1024").
  4) Route + model + capacity_tier labels (route="/chat-stream", model="redwood-v1", tier="dedicated").

elya: Example metrics and a PromQL starting point:

```
# histogram for kernel durations
redw_runtime_kernel_duration_seconds_bucket{kernel_name="tiled-matmul",route="/chat-stream",le="0.002"} 42

# token-level latency by phase
sum by (route,phase,kernel_name) (rate(redw_runtime_token_latency_seconds_sum[5m]))
```

# high-level derived query

```
# p95 TTFT per route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le,route) (rate(redw_runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{phase="ttft"}[10m])))
```

marta: Also add redw_kv_cache{route,model,result="hit|miss"} counters. We can compute an attributed TTFT delta by multiplying miss_count * avg_decode_time_on_miss.

derek: I want per-kernel p50/p95 on real traffic to see if selector oscillates (different kernels chosen across tokens in same request). Can we also add an index for kernel-selection-reason label (e.g., "shape_mismatch","quant_incompat","policy_fallback").

marta: Agree. Also propose a small set of histogram buckets for kernel durations: le={0.0001,0.0005,0.001,0.002,0.005,0.01}. Add logs for kernel-selection decisions with request-id and chosen_kernel for correlating traces.

simon: FYI I pushed a branch simon/kernel-fence that removed a small host-side memory fence introduced in commit abc123. That fence added ~80–120us before kernel launch at high concurrency. Might explain higher kernel-setup %.

elya: Ops plan:
  - Short term: ship the new metrics & counters behind a feature flag; deploy to canary pool.
  - Medium: add Grafana panels: TTFT waterfall (stacked phases), kernel heatmap (kernel_name vs seq_len), KV-attribution panel (misses -> expected TTFT delta).
  - Alerts: create an alert if p95(ttft) > 1.8s AND kv_miss_rate > 10% for 5m.
  - Debug step: run a targeted pbatch job that replays production batch-shape distribution and collect nvprof/pprof.

# debugging commands (examples)

```
# pprof on a running service heap/profile
go tool pprof -http=:8080 http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile

# quick nvprof sampling (on repro node)
nvprof --profile-from-start off --csv --print-gpu-trace ./inference_binary --replay-config shapes.json
```
deploy-bot: Rolling canary: metrics feature-flag -> canary pool-3. Config: ff=kernel-instr-v1 -> 10% of traffic. :rocket: 

derek: Great. Marta, can you sketch the Grafana panels and open a PR for metric names? We'll need to map these into downstream cost dashboards too.

marta: On it — I'll add dashboard mockups:
  - "TTFT waterfall (per-route)" — stacked bar per token phase, timeframe selector 5m/1h/24h.
  - "Kernel heatmap" — kernel_name (y) vs seq_len bins (x), color = p95 kernel_duration.
  - "KV attribution" — expected TTFT increase from misses, and raw kv_hit_rate timeseries.

elya: Also add labels for routing_policy and capacity_tier so we can test whether smart-routing fallbacks caused the selector churn.

simon: I'll run an AB replay with/without the fence change and attach pprof + kernel selection logs.

derek: Thanks everyone. If perf-bot sees the canary, please post an automated diff of p95(ttft) per-route after rollout.

perf-bot: Will post diff after 30m.

---
Notes: Keep metric names short and prefix with redw_ to avoid collisions. Avoid cardinality explosion: use coarse bins for batch shape (e.g., b1,b2-4,b5-16) rather than raw ints. Correlate with trace ids when investigating specific requests.
